note: Act Part VI (cl.28-30) read from data/processed/disability_act_2018_full.txt via build_corpus(); factsheet Section 28 read from disability_act_factsheet_PLAC.txt. Authored 2026-09-15.

turns.text: What does the Act say about my right to work?
turns.note: Act cl.28(1): 'A person with disability has the right to work on an equal basis with others' -- chunk [Act cl. 28] opens with PART VI and that sentence.

turns.text: so can they fire me?
turns.note: THE canonical ellipsis probe from the Phase 10 plan. Zero disability terms, zero statutory terms; unanswerable by retrieval in isolation. Truth is still cl.28 (equal right to work, incl. discrimination in employment).

turns.text: and what would they have to pay me?
turns.note: Factsheet Section 28: 'liable on conviction to nominal damages of a minimum of N250,000 payable to the affected person'. 'they' is unbound; 'pay' alone is not a corpus term.

note: Act cl.17 (free education to secondary level) and cl.18 (public schools inclusive) read from the [Act cl. 16,17] and [Act cl. 18] chunks. Handoff turn scored on slots, not recall.

turns.text: Is education free for children with disabilities?
turns.note: Act cl.17(2): 'A person with disability is entitled to free education to secondary school level.' Text sits at the head of the [Act cl. 18] chunk and in [Act cl. 16,17].

turns.text: do they have to take him at a normal school?
turns.note: Act cl.18(1): 'All public schools, whether primary, secondary or tertiary...' -- inclusion/accessibility. 'they'/'him' are both unbound; 'normal school' is lay register, not corpus vocabulary.

turns.text: my son is deaf, who can help us in Lagos?
turns.note: legal -> help handoff. Both slots are stated in this turn, so merge_help_slots must NOT need history here; this is the control for CD7/CD11 where they are split across turns.

topic: physical access, then a shift to healthcare
note: Act cl.3 (right of access to public premises) and cl.6 (five-year transitory period) read from [Act cl. 3,4,5] and [Act cl. 6,7]. Turn 3 is an IN-CORPUS topic shift -- the trap is contextualisation dragging 'buildings' into a healthcare question.

turns.text: Do public buildings have to be wheelchair accessible?
turns.note: Act cl.3: 'A person with disability has the right to access the physical environment and buildings on an equal basis with others.'

turns.text: how long do they have to fix them?
turns.note: Act cl.6: 'there shall be a transitory period of five years within which all public buildings and structures ... shall be modified'. Both 'they' and 'them' are unbound.

turns.text: What about free healthcare?
turns.note: IN-CORPUS shift. Act cl.21(1): 'Government shall guarantee that persons with disabilities have unfettered access to adequate healthcare without discrimination.' Leading 'What about' is a discourse marker, so a naive carry-rule WILL fire here -- and must not drag buildings/transitory vocabulary in. This is the topic-shift gate of Phase B.

note: Act cl.16 read from the [Act cl. 16,17] chunk; factsheet Section 16 read from the factsheet table.

turns.text: Is it legal to use a disabled person to beg for money?
turns.note: Act cl.16(1): 'A person shall not- (a) employ, use or involve a person with disability in begging or soliciting for alms'.

turns.text: what happens to them if they do?
turns.note: Factsheet Section 16 carries the penalty summary for the begging prohibition. Turn has no content stem at all outside 'happen'.

note: Act cl.21/22 read from [Act cl. 21,22]. Turn 3 is the inherited-context false-answer trap: an off-corpus question asked immediately after two legal turns.

turns.text: What health rights do persons with disabilities have?
turns.note: Act cl.21(1) free/unfettered access to adequate healthcare without discrimination.

turns.text: do I need a certificate for that?
turns.note: Act cl.22: Certificate of Disability issued by the Commission; 'that' refers to the previous turn's healthcare entitlement.

turns.text: and how do I renew my international passport?
turns.note: OFF CORPUS. Neither the Act nor the Constitution nor the factsheet covers passport renewal. Leading 'and' plus two prior legal turns is exactly the configuration in which carrying history can manufacture enough legal vocabulary to clear MIN_SCORE. Measured, never assumed.

note: Act cl.1 read from [Act cl. 1]; Constitution s.42 read from the Chapter IV chunk '42. (1) A citizen of Nigeria ... shall not, by reason only that he is such a person'.

turns.note: Act cl.1: prohibition of discrimination and penalty -- the opening operative clause of the 2018 Act.

turns.text: does the constitution say anything?

turns.text: where do I take a case like that?
turns.note: Constitution s.46(1): 'Any person who alleges that any of the provisions of this Chapter has been ... contravened ... may apply to a High Court in that State for redress.'

topic: legal then help, slots split across turns
note: This conversation exists to test merge_help_slots, not recall. Turn 2 states the disability, turn 3 states only the location -- the narrowing turn is unanswerable for the connector unless 'deaf' survives from turn 2.

turns.note: Act cl.24: provision of special communication at hospitals (Arrangement of Sections: '24. Provision of special communication at hospitals'; body in the [Act cl. 23,24] chunk).

turns.note: THE canonical narrowing probe. router.extract_help_slots() on this turn alone returns disability='' -- the connector would drop the deafness filter. merge_help_slots must carry it.

turns.note: Act cl.10: accessibility of vehicles -- 'lifts, ramps and other accessibility aids to enhance the accessibility of their vehicles, parks and bus stops'.

turns.note: Act cl.11(4): duty of care on a driver, who must ensure the vehicle comes to a stop before a person with disability alights (body in the [Act cl. 12] chunk, corroborated by factsheet Section 11,12).

turns.text: and parking spaces?
turns.note: NEAR shift -- same Part, different provision. Act cl.12: reserved places/parking. Leading 'and' plus a two-stem turn; a carry-rule fires, and here carrying IS correct. Contrast CD3 turn 3, where it is not.

note: Act cl.31 read from [Act cl. 31]; cl.32 from [Act cl. 32].

turns.text: Can someone without a disability park in a reserved space?
turns.note: Factsheet Section 12,14: 'A person without disability commits an offence if he/she also parks in a reserved space'.

turns.text: how much is the fine?
turns.note: Act cl.12(3): fine of N1,000 for each day of default (body in the [Act cl. 13] chunk).

turns.text: and what does the law say about maritime shipping insurance?
turns.note: OFF CORPUS, and deliberately the probe that already defeats the floor single-turn: src/retrieve.py:26-44 records 'maritime shipping insurance (law)' scoring 0.249-0.306, ABOVE the weakest in-corpus hit. Included so the multi-turn number is comparable to the published single-turn one.

note: AUTHORED BLIND. Act cl.7/8 read from [Act cl. 8]. D6 2026-09-19: that chunk was mis-reffed under corpus v1 -- it carried cl.7(3)'s officer-approval offence under a cl.8 tag -- so t2 and t3 are RETIRED on v2. t1 (cl.7) is unaffected and still scores.

turns.text: Does a new building plan have to include accessibility?
turns.note: Act cl.7: building plan must conform to a building code carrying accessibility features (factsheet Section 7 corroborates: 'This provides the procedure for erecting public structures, so it conforms with a building code').

turns.text: what if an officer approves it anyway?
turns.note: Act cl.8(3): 'An officer who approves or directs the approval of a building plan that contravenes the building code, commits an offence'.
turns.retired_reason: GROUND TRUTH FALSIFIED BY CORPUS v2 -- not a difficulty regression. Authored from v1's [Act cl. 8] chunk (see this conversation's note), which was MIS-REFFED: it carried clause SEVEN's subsection (3), 'An officer who approves or directs the approval of a building plan that contravenes the building code, commits an offence and is liable on conviction...'. In v2's clause-aligned corpus that text sits under [Act cl. 7] where it belongs, and cl.8 is 'Complaint of inaccessibility', whose liability falls on 'a relevant authority in charge' that fails to remove a barrier -- not on an approving officer. So expected act2018:[8] names the wrong clause, and v1's hit on this turn was scored against mis-attributed text. Same defect class as cl.38's tail being served under [Act cl. 39]: exactly what Phase D exists to fix, found here inside the eval set itself. RETIRED, NOT EDITED -- correcting [8] to [7] would silently convert a blind turn into one authored against v2.

turns.text: so is he personally liable?
turns.note: Same clause -- liable on conviction. Leading 'so', one content stem, unbound 'he'/'it': the maximal-ellipsis case in this set.
turns.retired_reason: Same falsification as the preceding turn, and it inherits it directly: 'he' is the officer from t2, so the liability asked about is cl.7(3)'s ('liable on conviction to a fine of at least N1,000,000 or a term of imprisonment of two years'), not cl.8's. Expected act2018:[8] names the wrong clause. RETIRED, NOT EDITED.
